candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: The friction factor cf is dimensionless by definition in fluid mechanics. The input variables are density (rho), dynamic viscosity (mu), pipe diameter (D), flow velocity (U), and roughness height (r). Density has dimensions of mass per volume, dynamic viscosity has dimensions of mass per length-time, diameter and roughness height are lengths, and velocity is length per time. The friction factor is known to be dimensionless, so all SI exponents are zero. The problem states the power of relative roughness height must be zero in the output formula, so the roughness height exponent is zero in the dimension vector for cf.

If any current coordinate is unknown, request revision or report UNCERTAIN; never call a partly known vector PASSED. Give a complete correction when physically justified. If a correction remains partly unknown, preserve null and explain what remains unresolved; the program will request revision rather than invent zeros. Lack of KB alone is not a physical contradiction. Matrix compilation and n/r/k are program tasks, not audit tasks.
